title: Toeplitz circulant and displacement structured solvers

items.title: Toeplitz, circulant, and finite-index conventions for structured solvers
items.statement:
All vector and matrix indices below start at $0$. A rectangular Toeplitz matrix $T\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$, where $m,n\ge1$, is specified by lags $t_r\in\mathbb C$ for $-(n-1)\le r\le m-1$ and has entries
$$T_{ij}:=t_{i-j}\qquad(0\le i<m,\ 0\le j<n).$$
For a square matrix $T\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, Hermitian Toeplitz means $t_{-r}=\overline{t_r}$ for $0\le r<n$. It is positive definite when $x^*Tx>0$ for every nonzero $x\in\mathbb C^n$, where $x^*:=\overline{x}^{\,T}$ and the product is the matrix product of [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]].

For $N\ge1$, a vector $c=(c_0,\ldots,c_{N-1})^T\in\mathbb C^N$ generates the circulant matrix
$$C(c)_{ij}:=c_{(i-j)\bmod N}\qquad(0\le i,j<N).$$
For $n\ge1$ and $0\le j<n$, let $e_j\in\mathbb C^n$ be the coordinate vector with $(e_j)_i=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. For $a\in\mathbb C^n$, $J_na$ is the reversed vector, $(J_na)_i=a_{n-1-i}$; $J_0$ is the unique map on the empty vector. The lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $L(a)\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with $L(a)_{ij}=a_{i-j}$ when $i\ge j$, and $0$ otherwise. The canonical unitary DFT is the map $\mathcal F_N$ of [[def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n]]; the unnormalised DFT used for operation counts is $D_N:=\sqrt N\,\mathcal F_N$.

These conventions specify matrix orientation, conjugation, normalization, and boundary indexing; in particular, circulant eigenvalues below use the negative-sign canonical DFT.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §§4.2.1 and 4.5.1
Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §2

items.title: A specified realified dense residual check bounds the exact residual
items.statement:
Let $s\ge1$, $A\in\mathbb R^{s\times s}$, $x,b\in\mathbb R^s$, and let each row dot product be evaluated left to right: round each product, then accumulate the rounded products from the first term onward. After computing $\widehat p=\operatorname{fl}(Ax)$, compute $\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(b-\widehat p)$ componentwise. Assume the standard relative model with unit roundoff $u$, all products, intermediate sums and subtractions are zero or in the normal range, and $(s+1)u<1$. Put $\gamma_q:=qu/(1-qu)$.

For the exact residual $r=b-Ax$, the specified operation DAG satisfies
$$|r-\widehat r|\le\gamma_{s+1}\bigl(|b|+|A||x|\bigr)$$
componentwise, and therefore
$$\|r\|_\infty\le\|\widehat r\|_\infty+ \gamma_{s+1}\bigl(\|b\|_\infty+\|A\|_\infty\|x\|_\infty\bigr),$$
where $\|A\|_\infty:=\max_i\sum_j|A_{ij}|$ and $\|x\|_\infty:=\max_i|x_i|$. If $d:=\|A\|_\infty\|x\|_\infty+\|b\|_\infty>0$, the normwise backward-error ratio $\eta_\infty:=\|r\|_\infty/d$ is at most $\gamma_{s+1}+\|\widehat r\|_\infty/d$; if $d=0$, then $r=0$.

For $n\ge1$, complex $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ and $x,b\in\mathbb C^n$, define $R_nz:=(\operatorname{Re}z,\operatorname{Im}z)^T\in\mathbb R^{2n}$ and $\mathcal R(A)=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}A&-\operatorname{Im}A\\\operatorname{Im}A&\operatorname{Re}A\end{pmatrix}$; put $\widetilde x=R_nx$ and $\widetilde b=R_nb$. The following square expresses the realification identity proved by direct multiplication in step 1.1.

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathbb C^n \arrow[r,"A"] \arrow[d,"R_n"'] & \mathbb C^n \arrow[d,"R_n"] \\
\mathbb R^{2n} \arrow[r,"\mathcal R(A)"] & \mathbb R^{2n}
\end{tikzcd}
```

Applying the same real DAG to $\mathcal R(A),\widetilde x,\widetilde b$ gives the same componentwise bound with $s=2n$ and the realified residual. This is a certificate for that explicit realified residual check; it is not a bound for an unspecified native complex-operation DAG or a solver-stability theorem.

references.title: David Bindel, CS 6210: Matrix Computations, Sums, Dots, and Error in Linear Systems

items.title: The canonical finite DFT diagonalizes every circulant
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, $c\in\mathbb C^N$, and let $C(c)$ be the circulant of [[def-toeplitz-circulant-and-displacement-notation]]. Put
$$\lambda_k:=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j e^{-2\pi i k j/N}=\sqrt N\,(\mathcal F_Nc)(k),\qquad 0\le k<N.$$
Then
$$C(c)=\mathcal F_N^{-1}\,\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{N-1})\,\mathcal F_N.$$
Consequently, $C(c)$ is invertible exactly when every $\lambda_k\ne0$. For $b\in\mathbb C^N$, $C(c)x=b$ is solvable exactly when $(\mathcal F_Nb)(k)=0$ for every zero mode $\lambda_k=0$; on nonzero modes every solution has $(\mathcal F_Nx)(k)=(\mathcal F_Nb)(k)/\lambda_k$, while its zero-mode coordinates are free.

The square records the identity $\mathcal F_NC(c)=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)\mathcal F_N$; the two paths send each input vector to the same Fourier-coordinate vector. The proof below establishes this identity from the finite convolution sums.

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathbb C^N \arrow[r,"C(c)"] \arrow[d,"\mathcal F_N"'] & \mathbb C^N \arrow[d,"\mathcal F_N"] \\
\mathbb C^N \arrow[r,"\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)"] & \mathbb C^N
\end{tikzcd}
```

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.2.1.6–4.2.1.14

items.title: A zero-padded circulant embedding computes a Toeplitz product in O(N log N)
items.statement:
Let $m,n\ge1$, let $T\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$ be Toeplitz with $T_{ij}=t_{i-j}$ for $0\le i<m$, $0\le j<n$, and let $x\in\mathbb C^n$. Set $L=m+n-1$ and let $N$ be the least power of two with $N\ge L$. Define $c\in\mathbb C^N$ by
$$c_\ell=t_\ell\ (0\le\ell<m),\qquad c_{N-d}=t_{-d}\ (1\le d<n),$$
and set every other coordinate to zero. Let $\widetilde x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1},0,\ldots,0)^T\in\mathbb C^N$. In exact arithmetic, the first $m$ coordinates of the cyclic convolution $c*_N\widetilde x$ equal $Tx$.

The convolution can be computed with three exact length-$N$ DFT calls, pointwise products, and scalar scaling. Its arithmetic count is $O(N\log_2N)$ for $N\ge2$ and constant when $N=1$. This is an exact-arithmetic count for the formal exact-constant FFT model; a finite-precision execution is not claimed to be exact.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.2
Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §1

items.title: Complex Hermitian Toeplitz bordering yields reflection coefficients and positive pivots
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $T_n=(t_{i-j})_{0\le i,j<n}$ be Hermitian positive definite, so $t_{-r}=\overline{t_r}$. For $0\le k\le n$, set $T_k=(t_{i-j})_{0\le i,j<k}$, with $T_0$ empty, and for $0\le k<n$ set $g_k=(t_1,\ldots,t_k)^T$, with $g_0$ empty. Define $\phi_0$ empty and $
u_0=t_0$. For each $0\le k\le n-2$, let $J_k$ reverse $k$ coordinates, put $c_k=J_k\overline{g_k}$, and set
$$\alpha_{k+1}:= rac{t_{k+1}-c_k^*\phi_k}{
u_k},\qquad \phi_{k+1}:= egin{pmatrix}\phi_k-J_k\overline{\phi_k}\,\alpha_{k+1}\ \alpha_{k+1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad 
u_{k+1}:=
u_k(1-|\alpha_{k+1}|^2).$$
Every denominator used is strictly positive; $T_k\phi_k=g_k$ and $
u_k=t_0-g_k^*\phi_k>0$ for $0\le k<n$. Computing through order $n-1$ takes $O(n^2)$ complex arithmetic operations and $O(n)$ working storage. This is the complex matrix-bordering extension; the real ACVF forecast procedure remains [[alg-durbin-levinson-forecast-recursion]].

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.341, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, Lecture 13: The Levinson-Durbin Recursion
Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3

items.title: Lower-shift displacement rank and generator pairs
items.statement:
For $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, let $Z=Z_n$ be the lower shift with $Z_{i+1,i}=1$ for $0\le i<n-1$ and all other entries zero. Its lower-shift (Stein) displacement is
$$\nabla_Z(A):=A-ZAZ^*.$$
The **displacement rank** of $A$ with respect to this fixed shift is $\operatorname{rank}(\nabla_Z(A))$. A pair of matrices $G,H\in\mathbb C^{n\times r}$ is a **generator of width $r$** when
$$\nabla_Z(A)=GH^*.$$
Such a factorization is a representation of the displacement, not a factorization of $A$ itself. The term **Toeplitz-like** refers to matrices whose displacement rank is small relative to $n$; the rank bound $r$ must be specified rather than unrestricted. For a family of growing dimensions, a uniform bound means that $r$ is independent of $n$. This definition makes no conditioning, pivot-growth, or numerical-stability assertion.

references.title: Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §2.1

items.title: General-RHS Hermitian Toeplitz solve by reflection recursion and Gohberg–Semencul
items.statement:
**Input:** An integer $n\ge1$, a Hermitian Toeplitz lag list $(t_{-(n-1)},\ldots,t_{n-1})$ satisfying $t_{-r}=\overline{t_r}$, and a right-hand side $b\in\mathbb C^n$. All arithmetic in this definition is exact. The real covariance forecast procedure remains [[alg-durbin-levinson-forecast-recursion]]; this procedure solves a general Hermitian matrix equation with arbitrary $b$.

**Output:** Either a vector $x\in\mathbb C^n$ or one of the statuses invalid-input, nonpositive-pivot(k), or zero-gohberg-semencul-denominator.

1. Reject invalid-input if the lag list or right-hand side has the wrong length, or if the Hermitian lag equalities fail. Set $T_{ij}=t_{i-j}$.
2. If $t_0\le0$, return nonpositive-pivot(0). Initialize $\phi_0$ empty and $\nu_0=t_0$. For $k=0,\ldots,n-2$, form $g_k=(t_1,\ldots,t_k)^T$, $c_k=J_k\overline{g_k}$, and
   $$\alpha_{k+1}=(t_{k+1}-c_k^*\phi_k)/\nu_k,\qquad \phi_{k+1}=(\phi_k-J_k\overline{\phi_k}\,\alpha_{k+1},\,\alpha_{k+1})^T,\qquad \nu_{k+1}=\nu_k(1-|\alpha_{k+1}|^2).$$
   If a required $\nu_k$ is not positive, return nonpositive-pivot(k) before dividing; if a newly computed $\nu_{k+1}\le0$, return nonpositive-pivot(k+1).
3. With $\phi=\phi_{n-1}$ and $\nu=\nu_{n-1}$, form
   $$v=(-J_{n-1}\overline{\phi}/\nu,\ 1/\nu)^T,\qquad u=J_n\overline v.$$
   If $u_0=0$, return zero-gohberg-semencul-denominator.
4. Do not form dense triangular matrices. For any $a,y\in\mathbb C^n$, compute
   $$(L(a)y)_i=\sum_{j=0}^{i}a_{i-j}y_j,\qquad (L(a)^*y)_i=\sum_{j=i}^{n-1}\overline{a_{j-i}}y_j.$$
   Return
   $$x=\bigl(L(u)L(u)^*b-L(Z_nv)L(Z_nv)^*b\bigr)/u_0,$$
   evaluating the four triangular products successively with vector workspace.

For a Hermitian positive-definite input, [[lem-complex-hermitian-toeplitz-reflection-recursion]] gives positive reflection pivots, so $u_0=1/\nu_{n-1}>0$. The formula is the complex Hermitian extension; it makes no finite-precision stability claim.

references.title: George Labahn and Tamir Shalom, Inversion of Toeplitz Matrices with Only Two Standard Equations, Theorem 1.1
Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3

items.title: A Toeplitz matrix has lower-shift displacement rank at most two
items.statement:
Let $T=(t_{i-j})_{0\le i,j<n}$ be any square Toeplitz matrix, and let $Z=Z_n$ be the lower shift of [[def-displacement-rank-generators-and-lower-shift]]. With $e_0=(1,0,\ldots,0)^T$ and $t_0=T_{00}$,
$$T-ZTZ^*=e_0(e_0^*T-t_0e_0^*)+(Te_0)e_0^*.$$
Consequently, its displacement rank is at most two. A width-two generator is
$$G=[\,e_0\ \ Te_0\,],\qquad H^*=\begin{bmatrix}e_0^*T-t_0e_0^*\\ e_0^*\end{bmatrix}.$$

references.title: Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §2.1
Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.1

items.title: One exact scalar elimination step updates a displacement generator
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$, let $A=\begin{pmatrix}d&r^*\\ \ell&M\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with $d\ne0$, and let $s\ge1$ be an integer. Let $Z_n=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\ e_0&Z_{n-1}\end{pmatrix}$ be the lower shift partitioned after its first row and column. Suppose
$$A-Z_nAZ_n^*=GH^*,\qquad G=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat G\\G_b\end{pmatrix},\quad H=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat H\\H_b\end{pmatrix},$$
where $G,H\in\mathbb C^{n\times s}$, $\widehat G,\widehat H\in\mathbb C^{1\times s}$, and $G_b,H_b\in\mathbb C^{(n-1)\times s}$. Let
$$S:=M-\ell d^{-1}r^*$$
be the scalar-pivot Schur complement. Define
$$p:=e_0+(Z_{n-1}\ell-\ell)/d,\qquad q:=e_0+(Z_{n-1}r-r)/\overline d,\qquad G':=G_b+p\widehat G,\quad H':=H_b+q\widehat H.$$
Then
$$S-Z_{n-1}SZ_{n-1}^*=G'H'^*.$$
Thus the updated displacement rank is at most $s$, although it can decrease. This is an exact identity conditional on the nonzero pivot $d$; it makes no conditioning or growth claim.

references.title: Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, Lemma 3.1

items.title: The Hermitian positive-definite Gohberg–Semencul formula is exact and quadratic
items.statement:
Let $T_n=(t_{i-j})_{0\le i,j<n}$ be Hermitian positive definite, and let $b\in\mathbb C^n$. Run [[alg-hermitian-toeplitz-general-rhs-gohberg-semencul-solve]] in exact arithmetic. It returns $x=T_n^{-1}b$. If $u=T_n^{-1}e_0$ and $v=T_n^{-1}e_{n-1}$ are the first and last inverse columns, then
$$T_n^{-1}=\frac1{u_0}\left(L(u)L(u)^*-L(Z_nv)L(Z_nv)^*\right),\qquad u_0>0.$$
The recursion and four triangular Toeplitz products use $O(n^2)$ complex arithmetic operations and $O(n)$ storage beyond the input, output, and lag vector. This is an exact-arithmetic cost statement and makes no finite-precision stability claim.

references.title: George Labahn and Tamir Shalom, Inversion of Toeplitz Matrices with Only Two Standard Equations, Theorem 1.1
Daniel Kressner and Robert Luce, Fast computation of the matrix exponential for a Toeplitz matrix, §§2–3.1

title: Toeplitz circulant and displacement structured solvers — Examples

items.title: The periodic Poisson circulant has one compatible zero mode
items.statement: For each $N\ge3$, let $C_N=C(c)$ be the periodic cycle Laplacian circulant generated by $c_0=2$, $c_1=-1$, $c_{N-1}=-1$, and $c_j=0$ otherwise. With $\omega=e^{-2\pi i/N}$, its Fourier eigenvalues are $\lambda_k=2-\omega^k-\omega^{-k}$. Exactly $\lambda_0$ vanishes, so $C_Nx=f$ is solvable exactly when $\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}f_j=0$; on the zero-mean subspace the solution is unique. For $N=4$ and $f=(1,-1,1,-1)^T$, the solution is $x=f/4$.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §§4.2.1 and 4.5.1

items.title: An invertible indefinite Toeplitz matrix triggers the pivot-failure branch
items.statement:
For the Hermitian Toeplitz matrix
$$T=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix},$$
the general-RHS solver reports a nonpositive second pivot, even though $T$ is invertible. The status records that the solver's HPD domain condition failed; it does not claim that the indefinite system has no solution.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3
MIT OpenCourseWare 6.341, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, Lecture 13: The Levinson-Durbin Recursion

items.title: An AR(1) covariance forecast and general-RHS Toeplitz solve
items.statement:
Assume a real, mean-zero, weakly stationary process $X_t$ satisfies the causal AR(1) model
$$X_t=\tfrac12X_{t-1}+\varepsilon_t$$
in $L^2$, where $\varepsilon_t$ is centered with variance $3/4$, is uncorrelated with $X_s$ for every $s<t$, and the process is weakly stationary. Here “AR(1)” means precisely this first-order autoregression; the stated uncorrelatedness is the innovation orthogonality used below. Then its autocovariance function (ACVF) is $\gamma(h)=2^{-|h|}$. The order-two Durbin–Levinson output is $\phi_2=(1/2,0)^T$ and $\nu_2=3/4$. Separately, for $T=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=(1,1)^T$, the general-RHS Hermitian Toeplitz solver returns $T^{-1}b=(2/3,2/3)^T$ by the Gohberg–Semencul formula.

references.title: Ralf Hiptmair, Numerical Methods for Computational Science and Engineering, Lecture Document, §4.5.3
MIT OpenCourseWare 6.341, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, Lecture 13: The Levinson-Durbin Recursion
